transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-03
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood), Tomás Ruiz (Aurora), Priya Singh (Aurora), Evan Liu (Aurora)

Summary: quick partner intro, high-level go-to-market and technical discovery for potential integration. Discussed VPC/on-prem connectivity, KMS, compliance, GPU types (A100/H100), pilot metrics, and co-sell motion. Next steps and owners at end.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya Chen from Redwood Inference, I'm the AE on this motion. We've got Ravi and Lena from our solutions team with me. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Tomás: Good, thanks Maya. Tomás here, Head of Integrations at Aurora. Priya and Evan are with me. We were excited to connect and understand how Redwood might fit into our partner offering.
[00:14] Priya: Hey all, quick note we run a mix of cloud and some customer on-prem installs — lots of telco and finance accounts.
[00:20] Ravi: Great, thanks. Quick agenda — intros, what Aurora offers, high-level Redwood product map, then a technical check on connectivity, security, and pilot scope. Sound good?
[00:28] Evan: Sounds good.
[00:32] Maya: Perfect. Tomás, could you give a 2 minute overview of Aurora's integration business?
[00:37] Tomás: Sure, yes. We surface GPU-backed inference as a managed integration into our customers, we do orchestration, scheduling, and have a marketplace for model bundles. We target medium/enterprise customers that need both cloud and air-gapped on-prem options, lots of regulatory constraints. Usually customers pick our managed stack or we deploy inside their VPC. We're exploring partnering with Redwood for a few reasons — your runtime optimizations and the unified API we can present to customers.
[00:56] Maya: Nice, thanks. A little about Redwood: we provide hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private deployments — same API across each. Our differentiator is production-first runtime optimizations, smart routing, caching + quantization suggestions, and observability. Ravi, want to add on the runtime side?
[01:14] Ravi: Yeah — our runtime supports continuous batching, KV cache (sometimes transcribed as "K V cash"), and kernel selection for A100/H100 and some ARM-based options. We do quantization-friendly paths; so if a workload benefits from int8 or q4 profiles we can recommend those for cost. For partners we often map a partner pool — dedicated capacity behind a partner account — or integrate via VPC peering for private deployments.
[01:39] Priya: Two quick things from our side — certification/compliance is huge: SOC 2 and ISO are required for many of our accounts, and we also need audit logs and SSO/SAML. Second, for on-prem we need a small footprint that can run without NVLink assumptions.
[01:54] Lena: That's totally fair. We have SOC 2 Type II and are working through ISO in our 2026 roadmap; we can share certs. Audit logs and KMS integration (we support customer-managed KMS/HSM for private deploys) are available. For on-prem we have an appliance packaging model and a 'private control plane' that can run disconnected — customers manage keys. Sometimes the transcription of that gets messy but we'll send the doc.
[02:21] Tomás: When you say private control plane — is that full UI/console access in our VPC or do you still call back to Redwood? Some customers require zero egress.
[02:30] Ravi: Good question. We offer a fully private deployment where the control plane sits in the customer's network — no egress required — as well as a hybrid mode where telemetry can be optionally sent. For zero egress we do an on-prem package and KMS integration. We'll follow up with the exact network topology doc.
[02:45] Evan: For VPC peering — do you support AWS, GCP, Azure direct peering? And do you require transit gateways?
[02:52] Maya: Yes to AWS/GCP/Azure; the specifics vary. For high-throughput partners we often recommend direct peering or private link equivalents. Transit gateway is optional; we can support both peering and VPC endpoints depending on region. We'll attach a sample diagram.
[03:05] Priya: Excellent. Another technical constraint: some customers insist on a specific GPU family — mostly H100 preferred but A100 still common. Do you have tested performance profiles?
[03:15] Ravi: We maintain a model catalog with verified performance profiles per GPU type and sequence length. For H100 vs A100 we have kernel selection tuned. We can share our benchmark sheet — it's usually NVMe and kernel-sensitive for long contexts. If you have a target model we can run a quick benchmark during the pilot.
[03:34] Tomás: That's helpful. On billing — Aurora wants a reseller/partner pricing model, possibly a revenue share or committed capacity arrangement. Is that something Redwood does?
[03:44] Maya: Yes, we have partner programs — revenue share, reseller discounts, and reserved capacity bookings. For Dedicated/reserved we can do monthly commits and partner pricing. We'll pass the partner program doc and legal starter language.
[03:55] Tomás: Nice. For pilots, we usually want to see cost per token and latency SLOs at 99th percentile with our traffic shape — like a mix of short chat and longer retrieval-augmented requests. Typical target: p99 < 500ms for short chats and reasonable cost.
[04:12] Ravi: That's reasonable. We can replicate that in our pilot with a staged dataset and your traffic profile. For latency SLOs we'll look at batching configs, KV cache hit rates, and routing to lower-latency variants.
[04:26] Priya: On security: can we map user access via SSO/SAML to RBAC in Redwood Console? We need audit trail per partner account.
[04:33] Lena: Yes, SAML SSO + RBAC is supported. Audit logging includes token-level tracing — cost/latency per token — and we can retain logs to match your retention policy as an add-on.
[04:45] Evan: Network question: do you support TLS mTLS for peered endpoints?
[04:49] Ravi: We do. Mutual TLS + IP whitelisting and optional client certs for VPC endpoints. We'll include specifics in the network doc.
[05:00] Tomás: Great. Switching to integration UX — we want to offer Redwood as an optional backend in our marketplace. Ideally one API surfaced through Aurora's console and then pointer to Redwood as execution plane. How hard is mapping routing rules and model variants?
[05:12] Maya: We have programmatic APIs and routing policies — you can set rules by latency, cost, region, and have fallback to compatible model variants. Many partners implement a simple pointer in their UI and then use our SDK to manage keys and fallbacks. It's pretty standard.
[05:28] Priya: Do you have webhook/callbacks for job completion and usage events?
[05:31] Ravi: Yes webhooks, and we also have tracing hooks for per-request metadata. You can ingest these into your billing pipeline.
[05:38] Tomás: One of our engineering concerns is multi-tenancy — we want to ensure strict isolation between our customers if they share the same Redwood pool. Can we have per-tenant encryption keys?
[05:46] Lena: Yes, per-tenant KMS mapping is possible. In Dedicated scenarios we allocate isolated pools and you control keys. For hosted partner pools we can enforce logical isolation with per-tenant keys and RBAC.
[05:58] Priya: Operationally, how does incident response work for partners?
[06:02] Maya: We have partner SLAs and dedicated support escalation paths. For Dedicated or Private customers we offer a named technical account manager and playbooks for incident triage. We'll include our SLAs and the contact model.
[06:14] Evan: Can Redwood run in disconnected air-gapped mode for on-prem? Some of our customers are strict.
[06:19] Ravi: Yes, we have an air-gapped on-prem package. No external egress required, and we support local KMS/HSM. We do recommend occasional secured updates for security patches but that can be scheduled per customer's policy.
[06:34] Tomás: Excellent. Anything on model licensing? Some customers want to use commercial LLMs; others prefer open models. How do you support different model ops?
[06:43] Ravi: We support open model catalog and can also run licensed models if you bring the license or through a managed contract. We handle model variants and version pinning to ensure reproducibility. For some proprietary models we might need a dedicated pool depending on license terms.
[06:59] Priya: For co-sell, we typically want marketing materials and joint case studies. Do you have a partner co-marketing program?
[07:06] Maya: Yes, partner co-marketing is part of our program — joint webinars, solution briefs, and a featured listing in our partner catalog for committed partners. We'll send the partner program deck.
[07:17] Tomás: Okay, technical follow-up: what's the onboarding time to get a partner pool live, assuming we want dedicated capacity?
[07:24] Maya: Typically 2-4 weeks for a basic reserved partner pool with our standard onboarding — longer if there are custom on-prem packaging or compliance gates. We can accelerate if you provide network and compliance info early.
[07:36] Evan: During pilot, we'd like to run a 2-week benchmark: 1k rps sustained for short chat traffic, and some long RAG queries. Can Redwood simulate and provide p50/p95/p99?
[07:47] Ravi: Absolutely. We'll provision a temporary dedicated pool for the pilot and run synthetic loads plus your real dataset. We'll provide latency breakdowns and token cost estimates.
[07:58] Priya: On integrations, is there an SDK for our marketplace that hides token handling for end customers?
[08:03] Lena: Yes, SDKs in Python/Node/Go — we also have a server-side proxy pattern for marketplaces so you don't surface raw tokens to end users.
[08:12] Tomás: Any gotchas with long context windows and KV cache for RAG workflows?
[08:17] Ravi: The main gotcha is cache invalidation and memory growth for very long live sessions — we provide KV cache eviction policies and monitoring. For very long contexts, kernel selection and memory footprint vary by model and quantization. We'll advise per model.
[08:30] Maya: Quick note — our Optimize product can suggest batching and quantization profiles for specific workloads which often reduces cost by 30-50% in early pilots.
[08:41] Tomás: That could be compelling for customers sensitive to cost.
[08:44] Priya: Ok, let's talk legal and procurement briefly. We'll need a starter contract and data processing addendum for data residency. Any special clauses around ephemeral logging?
[08:55] Maya: We can provide a template SOW and DPA. Ephemeral logging can be configured — we support zero-retention options for sensitive customers. We'll flag that in the security packet.
[09:06] Evan: In terms of real-world perf numbers, can you share a sample for a 7B and a 70B open model on A100 and H100? Even ballpark is helpful.
[09:16] Ravi: We'll share a benchmark spreadsheet but ballpark: 7B on A100 often hits ~30-70 ms per token depending on batch, 70B on H100 could be 60-200 ms per token depending on optimized kernels and batch. There's a lot of variance per prompt shape.
[09:33] Tomás: Great. Any concerns about model drift monitoring / quality regression?
[09:38] Lena: We have quality monitoring and eval hooks tied to prompt sets. You can set regression alerts when outputs fall below thresholds. Useful during rollouts.
[09:48] Priya: Finally for the pilot we need: (1) partner KB + network diagram, (2) partner pricing + reseller terms, (3) pilot plan and metrics template.
[09:57] Maya: We'll send those. Also propose a timeline: send docs by 6/5, pilot kickoff week of 6/8, benchmark results two weeks after.
[10:05] Tomás: That timeline works. Anything else on features or integrations?
[10:10] Evan: One last Q — for model repositories, does Redwood host containerized models or do you pull from our registry?
[10:17] Ravi: Both. We can host model artifacts or pull from your private registry. For on-prem air-gapped we typically ingest a tarball and register locally.
[10:25] Priya: Good. That's all from our side.
[10:28] Maya: Awesome — quick recap then next steps. Recap: Redwood to provide partner and security packet, network diagram, pilot plan and a benchmark sheet; Aurora to provide traffic profile and compliance contacts. Owners: Maya, Ravi, Tomás.
[10:42] Tomás: Yep, we'll get those over. Thanks everyone.
[10:45] Maya: Thanks all. We'll follow up by email with the docs and propose the kickoff time.

(Transcription notes: a few names and acronyms may be slightly mis-transcribed; some technical terms like KV cache showed up as "K V cash" in auto-transcript.)
